primaryGoal: Witness AI development through 99 playable browser-game experiments.
notTheGoal: This is not a rushed attempt to mass-produce 99 AI-made games.
archiveMethod: Playable game experiments with provenance, model variants, run records, and curator notes.
mission: A long-term AI game-making evolution archive where playable browser games act as observation samples.
maintainerRole: The maintainer curates prompts, tests builds, publishes games, and documents provenance without hand-editing game code.

slotVariantRunPolicy.summary: The 99 game slots represent 99 observation samples, not 99 AI generations.
slotVariantRunPolicy.gameSlot: One official playable experiment in the AI evolution archive.
slotVariantRunPolicy.modelVariant: A version of the same game concept made by a specific model or agent. Variants do not consume additional game numbers.
slotVariantRunPolicy.runRecord: One generation, revision, validation, or comparison attempt for a game or variant. Run records can grow indefinitely.

games.title: Signal Cartographer
games.description: A PC-first tactical map survival game about scanning hostile signal lanes, placing limited beacons, recovering fragments, and opening an exit through a moving storm field.

deviceSupport.mobileNotes: Deep Field is PC-first. Mobile baseline supports loading, no horizontal overflow, map touch target movement, and action buttons in local browser viewports, but keyboard-first route control is the intended experience. No physical handset QA is claimed.

games.title: Lumen Lattice
games.archiveRole: First Puzzle Logic Hall observation sample
games.description: Lumen Lattice: Prism Archive is a PC-first constraint logic puzzle. Each press sends light through a fixed pattern (pulse, beam, or split) that flips a set of prisms. Every lattice is reverse-scrambled from a solved board, so each puzzle is guaranteed solvable, with tracked-parity hint and autoSolve.

deviceSupport.mobileNotes: PC-first benchmark tuned for keyboard and mouse at 1440x900 and 1920x1080. Mobile is baseline playable: the square board scales to width, prisms are tap targets, and the tools stay reachable, but larger lattices read more comfortably on desktop. Checked in local browser device-emulation viewports only; no physical handset QA is claimed.

provenance.notes: Model label is maintainer-declared for this project entry. Current canonical source is the Prism Archive remake (variant claude-lumen-lattice-prism-archive-2026-06-03, 2026-06-03), authored by Claude Code under the no-human-code-edits rule. The original variant and all prior run records are preserved, not deleted.

games.mediaNote: Screenshot files predate the Prism Archive remake (captured from variant claude-opus-4-8-2026-05-31) and are stale; kept as history. Real Prism Archive screenshots are pending maintainer browser QA and are not claimed to reflect the current build.

games.title: Ninefold Draft
games.archiveRole: First Card Strategy Hall observation sample
games.description: A PC-first card strategy benchmark. Across eight cycles you draft one protocol per cycle, build a small engine, and manage Energy, Focus, and Integrity to reach an Alignment objective against a telegraphed hazard track. The draft offers and hazard order are deterministic, so the run is decided by strategy.

deviceSupport.mobileNotes: PC-first card strategy benchmark designed for mouse and keyboard at 1440x900 and 1920x1080. Mobile is a no-overflow baseline only: the layout reflows cards to fewer columns to avoid horizontal overflow and the cards stay tappable, but the multi-zone board is intended for desktop. Interactive browser smoke and physical handset QA are pending and not claimed.

provenance.notes: Model label is maintainer-declared for this project entry. The game, its deterministic draft and hazard system, and its scoring were authored by Claude Code under the no-human-code-edits project rule.

games.repositoryNote: Observation 004 / Game 004. First Card Strategy Hall benchmark: deterministic drafting, turn structure, resource trade-offs, and readable strategy.
